title: GitHub - harelix/aiport: A self-improving local LLM gateway for the polymorphic vibe coder
excerpt: A self-improving local LLM gateway for the polymorphic vibe coder - harelix/aiport
content_html:
Who it is for

If you're an erratic vibe coder, you know the day: Claude Code in one repo, Codex in another, a model on Ollama or llama.cpp, and credits on Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta. You switch models by task, sometimes mid-task, and jump between projects several times an hour. The apps you build call those models too, so each one ends up re-wiring the same providers. You can't see which app called what, and you find out about failures when something breaks.

aiport is a Go program that runs on your machine (loopback only) and sits between your apps, your coding agents and the providers.

The basics

  • One client per app. One OpenAI-style or Anthropic-style client, pointed at aiport, instead of setup code per provider.
  • Keys stay in aiport. Provider keys live in a private env file (mode 0600, plain text, never in the YAML config). Each app and agent gets its own revocable token. An app's coding agent connects it, and you approve a short pairing code.
  • Agents without your keys. aiport agent claude or aiport agent codex launches an agent with its own token, so it never sees your provider keys.
  • Name the need. Apps name a model, ask for fast, balanced or best, or name a task and an effort.

The part that improves over time

aiport watches how your apps use models and proposes changes. Nothing is applied without your approval unless you turn that on, and every change can be reverted.

  • Compression with a quality check. Apps can opt in to smaller prompts. aiport tracks answer quality per compression method and shows a verdict for each: no harm seen, possible harm, or not enough data.
  • Routing from human feedback. Thumbs up and down from your app's users become suggestions for which model should handle which requests.
  • Self-healing apps. Repeated failures are grouped into Issues, each with a fix on both sides: a change to aiport for you to approve, and instructions for the app's coding agent. Fix it can also run a coding agent in a separate git worktree. You review the diff, and if you keep it, aiport commits it on a new branch. aiport never commits to your branch, merges or pushes.
  • Minimal observability, on purpose. Every call is logged as metadata only: app, model, effort, latency, status and failure reason. Prompts and responses are never stored. That's enough to drive the loop above without keeping your data.

Design choices and limits

  • Native formats. Requests pass through in each provider's native format with no translation, to avoid lossy conversion of tool calls and streaming. The trade-off is that a client only reaches providers that speak its protocol.
  • Single user by design. No teams or budgets. LiteLLM, Portkey or Bifrost fit those needs better.

How it works

flowchart LR
  A["Applications<br/>and coding agents"] -- "own aiport token" --> G(("aiport"))
  G -- "provider key added" --> P["Providers<br/>OpenAI · Anthropic · Bedrock · Meta<br/>Ollama · llama.cpp"]
  G -. "Issues and Suggestions" .-> O["You, in the dashboard"]
  O -. "approve, revert" .-> G
Loading

Applications call aiport with their own token. aiport routes each call to the provider you chose, keeps the metadata, and turns repeated failures into Issues you can fix from the dashboard, or hand to the application's coding agent.

Quickstart

You need Go 1.27+ (brew install go, or go.dev/dl). Dependencies are vendored and the dashboard is pre-built, so nothing else is downloaded.

git clone https://github.com/harelix/aiport && cd aiport
make build              # bin/aiport, dashboard included
./bin/aiport init       # choose providers and coding agents; writes aiport.yaml
./bin/aiport serve      # prints the dashboard address and management token

Or install the binary without cloning: go install github.com/harelix/aiport/cmd/aiport@latest (it lands in $(go env GOPATH)/bin; run aiport init and aiport serve).

Open the dashboard address serve prints (http://127.0.0.1:8787/ by default; init --listen picks another, and you can use aiport.localhost instead), paste the management token and set a password. Paste your provider keys on Providers, then Check connection on each card: it makes one free GET /models call and generates nothing. Start any local provider (Ollama, llama.cpp) yourself.

Using it

  • Connect an application. On Integrate, open Instructions at the top and copy them to the coding agent working on the application. It switches the application's SDK to http://127.0.0.1:8787 and pairs it; you approve the short code it shows. The application's token goes in a gitignored .aiport file at its repository root, read by both the application and its coding agent; New token replaces a lost one and the trash icon removes an application. See Connect.
  • Launch a coding agent through aiport. ./bin/aiport agent claude --model MODEL or ./bin/aiport agent codex --model MODEL (add --dry-run to inspect). The agent gets its own token, never your provider keys.
  • Decide on Changes. Issues, Suggestions and Change requests wait on Changes, with a badge only when one needs you. Every Change can be reverted.

The manual covers every page. It is also built into the dashboard: press the help button, or the ⓘ next to any section.

Configuration

init writes aiport.yaml and a private aiport.yaml.env (mode 0600) for local tokens and the keys you paste in the dashboard. It never overwrites a file, and provider keys never go into YAML.

./bin/aiport init --provider openai,anthropic --agent codex,claude   # without prompts
./bin/aiport check                                                    # validate the configuration
./bin/aiport auth token                                               # print the management token again

Provider presets: openai, anthropic, bedrock, meta, ollama, llamacpp. See the configuration reference and aiport.example.yaml.

Security and data

  • Calls go only to the providers you configured, with that provider's key. aiport stores request metadata (time, application, model, status, latency), never prompts or responses.
  • Agent runs start a coding agent you installed (Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI) in a separate git worktree, only when you click. Commands ask you first, and aiport never commits to your branch, merges or pushes. An agent's own settings can allow more than aiport sees: read what aiport cannot see first.
  • Extensions you add take part in decisions about Change requests.
  • Found a vulnerability? Report it privately as SECURITY.md describes, not in a public issue.

Limitations

aiport is experimental. No provider and coding-agent combination has passed the live compatibility gate yet. Token counts and cost are not measured. A provider must speak the protocol of the client calling it, since aiport does not translate. Gemini runs' model calls do not go through aiport, and Codex runs use Codex's own login. There are no release downloads yet; build from source.

Contributing

aiport is maintained by one person in their spare time: issues and pull requests are read, but replies are best effort and may take a while. See CONTRIBUTING.md and the code of conduct. CI runs on every push; locally, run make test, make check and make check-offline, and sign off every commit (DCO). Larger changes start from the design; the vocabulary is in the glossary, and dependency licenses are in THIRD_PARTY.md.

License

Apache-2.0. The aiport name and logo are covered by TRADEMARKS.md.

  • Routing from human feedback. Thumbs up and down from your app's users become suggestions for which model should handle which requests.
  • Self-healing apps. Repeated failures are grouped into Issues, each with a fix on both sides: a change to aiport for you to approve, and instructions for the app's coding agent. Fix it can also run a coding agent in a separate git worktree. You review the diff, and if you keep it, aiport commits it on a new branch. aiport never commits to your branch, merges or pushes.
  • Minimal observability, on purpose. Every call is logged as metadata only: app, model, effort, latency, status and failure reason. Prompts and responses are never stored. That's enough to drive the loop above without keeping your data.

Design choices and limits

  • Native formats. Requests pass through in each provider's native format with no translation, to avoid lossy conversion of tool calls and streaming. The trade-off is that a client only reaches providers that speak its protocol.
  • Single user by design. No teams or budgets. LiteLLM, Portkey or Bifrost fit those needs better.

它是如何运作的

flowchart LR
  A["Applications<br/>and coding agents"] -- "own aiport token" --> G(("aiport"))
  G -- "provider key added" --> P["Providers<br/>OpenAI · Anthropic · Bedrock · Meta<br/>Ollama · llama.cpp"]
  G -. "Issues and Suggestions" .-> O["You, in the dashboard"]

Loading

Applications call aiport with their own token. aiport routes each call to the provider you chose, keeps the metadata, and turns repeated failures into Issues you can fix from the dashboard, or hand to the application's coding agent.

快速入门

You need Go 1.27+ (brew install go, or go.dev/dl). Dependencies are vendored and the dashboard is pre-built, so nothing else is downloaded.

git clone https://github.com/harelix/aiport && cd aiport
make build              # bin/aiport, dashboard included
./bin/aiport init       # choose providers and coding agents; writes aiport.yaml
./bin/aiport serve      # prints the dashboard address and management token

Or install the binary without cloning: go install github.com/harelix/aiport/cmd/aiport@latest (it lands in $(go env GOPATH)/bin; run aiport init and aiport serve).

Open the dashboard address serve prints (http://127.0.0.1:8787/ by default; init --listen picks another, and you can use aiport.localhost instead), paste the management token and set a password. Paste your provider keys on Providers, then Check connection on each card: it makes one free GET /models call and generates nothing. Start any local provider (Ollama, llama.cpp) yourself.

使用它

  • Connect an application. On Integrate, open Instructions at the top and copy them to the coding agent working on the application. It switches the application's SDK to http://127.0.0.1:8787 and pairs it; you approve the short code it shows. The application's token goes in a gitignored .aiport file at its repository root, read by both the application and its coding agent; New token replaces a lost one and the trash icon removes an application. See Connect.
  • Launch a coding agent through aiport. ./bin/aiport agent claude --model MODEL or ./bin/aiport agent codex --model MODEL (add --dry-run to inspect). The agent gets its own token, never your provider keys.
  • Decide on Changes. Issues, Suggestions and Change requests wait on Changes, with a badge only when one needs you. Every Change can be reverted.

The manual covers every page. It is also built into the dashboard: press the help button, or the ⓘ next to any section.

配置

init writes aiport.yaml and a private aiport.yaml.env (mode 0600) for local tokens and the keys you paste in the dashboard. It never overwrites a file, and provider keys never go into YAML.

./bin/aiport init --provider openai,anthropic --agent codex,claude   # without prompts
./bin/aiport check                                                    # validate the configuration
./bin/aiport auth token                                               # print the management token again

Provider presets: openai, anthropic, bedrock, meta, ollama, llamacpp. See the configuration reference and aiport.example.yaml.

Security and data

  • Calls go only to the providers you configured, with that provider's key. aiport stores request metadata (time, application, model, status, latency), never prompts or responses.
  • Agent runs start a coding agent you installed (Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI) in a separate git worktree, only when you click. Commands ask you first, and aiport never commits to your branch, merges or pushes. An agent's own settings can allow more than aiport sees: read what aiport cannot see first.
  • Extensions you add take part in decisions about Change requests.
  • 发现漏洞？ Report it privately as SECURITY.md describes, not in a public issue.

局限性

aiport is experimental. No provider and coding-agent combination has passed the live compatibility gate yet. Token counts and cost are not measured. A provider must speak the protocol of the client calling it, since aiport does not translate. Gemini runs' model calls do not go through aiport, and Codex runs use Codex's own login. There are no release downloads yet; build from source.

贡献

aiport is maintained by one person in their spare time: issues and pull requests are read, but replies are best effort and may take a while. See CONTRIBUTING.md and the code of conduct. CI runs on every push; locally, run make test, make check and make check-offline, and sign off every commit (DCO). Larger changes start from the design; the vocabulary is in the glossary, and dependency licenses are in THIRD_PARTY.md.
